Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your baby has bilious vomiting and cannot pass meconium, which causes abdominal distension. This combination of symptoms is very concerning for a lower intestinal obstruction.

I need to ask a few questions to narrow down the cause. First, were you able to see any stool or just mucus when you wiped your baby's bottom after birth?

Also, has your baby passed gas, or has the abdomen become hard or scaphoid?

Given the bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium, and abdominal distension, I need to know if you notice any colored streaks in the vomit or if the baby has had episodes of violent crying suggesting severe pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound results showing normal readings make malrotation with volvulus unlikely, so we are focusing on distal obstructions like Hirschsprung's disease or meconium ileus. Has your baby's family history included any bowel issues, and are there any specific genetic syndromes in the maternal lineage?

REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Enema (to assess for the "transition zone" typical of Hirschsprung's).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Rectal enema demonstrates a narrowed distal segment with an abrupt transition to proximal dilated bowel loops, consistent with the transition zone seen in Hirschsprung's disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The rectal enema findings of a narrowed distal segment with an abrupt transition to dilated loops are classic for Hirschsprung's disease. Given the confirmed distal obstruction, bilious vomiting, and failure to pass meconium, I am confident in this diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's Disease
